comparison: Strong agreement on geraniol binding to central hydrophobic pocket (C33-C37). Both evaluations find ITC and cryo-EM data compelling and support the identification of this novel binding site. OpenEval emphasizes stoichiometry consistency while peer reviewers highlight this as a key strength with no concerns raised.

Strong agreement on peptide dimer development and binding characterization (C38-C44). Both evaluations support the nanomolar affinity findings and sequence-activity relationships. OpenEval details fold-change calculations and microarray data, while peer reviewers specifically praise the P1-dimer nanomolar affinity as a strength.

Strong agreement on cryo-EM structural confirmation (C53-C54, C64-C65). Both evaluations support the structural characterization of binding sites and peptide density at spike tips. OpenEval emphasizes differential binding to quasi-equivalent sites, while peer reviewers praise the combination of cryo-EM with other techniques.

Strong agreement on in vitro aggregation effects (C6, C66-C68). Both evaluations support turbidity assay and cryo-EM aggregation data. OpenEval emphasizes correlation between binding affinity and aggregation potency across multiple assays, while peer reviewers acknowledge the demonstrated in vitro aggregation effects.

Strong agreement on cellular aggregation effects (C47-C48). Both evaluations support fluorescence microscopy data showing HBc aggregation in cells. OpenEval emphasizes the negative control with scrambled peptide, while peer reviewers praise the cellular demonstration enabled by cell-penetrating peptide grafting.

Agreement on ligand-specific conformational effects (C57-C60). Both evaluations support the structural observations about geraniol not inducing Phe97 flipping. OpenEval provides detailed structural comparisons, while peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the compelling experimental framework without raising concerns.

Agreement on background and contextual claims about HBV burden and treatment landscape (C1-C2, C8-C11, C14-C18, C71). Both evaluations support these established knowledge claims. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate citations and consistency, while peer reviewers accept these as unquestioned scientific foundation.

Agreement on HBV treatment mechanisms and CAM rationale (C12-C13, C19-C25, C69-C70). Both evaluations support these background claims. OpenEval highlights well-cited structural and mechanistic information, while peer reviewers accept these contextual claims without question as part of the manuscript rationale.

Agreement on prior work establishing alternative HBc binding sites (C26-C32). Both evaluations support these literature-based claims. OpenEval emphasizes citations providing rationale for exploring these sites, while peer reviewers accept these as part of the established scientific context.

Both address main findings summary (C3-C5). OpenEval R9 groups summary claims together and links them to experimental data (C33-C54). Peer R1 addresses C3 specifically about novel binding pockets along with the supporting experimental claims. Both find these claims supported by ITC and cryo-EM data.

Partial overlap on main findings. OpenEval R9 includes C4 (peptide dimer binding) as part of summary claims supported by experimental data. Peer R2 addresses C4 along with detailed peptide characterization claims (C38-C46). Both evaluations support the peptide dimer findings.

Partial overlap on structural confirmation. OpenEval R9 includes C5 (cryo-EM confirmation) as part of summary claims. Peer R3 addresses C5 along with specific structural characterization claims (C53-C55, C64-C65). Both evaluations support the cryo-EM structural data.

Partial overlap on aggregation observations. OpenEval R7 includes cryo-EM aggregate observations (C49-C51) as part of structural characterization. Peer R4 addresses these claims in context of in vitro aggregation effects (C6, C66-C68). Both evaluations support the aggregation findings.

Minimal overlap on cellular effects. OpenEval R8 includes C7 (cellular aggregation) as part of broader aggregation analysis with turbidity and cryo-EM data. Peer R5 focuses specifically on cellular aggregation (C7, C47-C48). Both evaluations support the cellular findings.

Minimal overlap on P1dC characterization. OpenEval R6 addresses P1dC affinity and cellular aggregation (C45-C48). Peer R2 includes C45-C46 as part of broader peptide dimer characterization (C38-C46). Both evaluations support the P1dC binding data.

Agreement on supporting structural and methodological claims (C56, C61-C63). Both evaluations support these contextual claims about capsid characterization and cited literature. OpenEval emphasizes structural comparisons, while peer reviewers accept these as part of the experimental framework without concerns.
